claim: The CDC released 148 pages relating to its myocarditis follow-up work with every word blacked out. The pages were produced to Epoch Times reporter Zachary Stieber under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), concerning the agency's MOVING project — Myocarditis Outcomes After mRNA COVID-19 Vaccination — and each page carried the marking '(b)(5)', the FOIA exemption for 'inter-agency or intra-agency memorandums or letters which would not be available by law to a party other than an agency in litigation with the agency.' On March 15, 2024, Arizona state senator Janae Shamp displayed the printed stack while chairing the legislature's Novel Coronavirus Southwestern Intergovernmental Committee, at which Dr. Peter McCullough was seated as a committee member. Two things follow that are usually reported separately. The (b)(5) deliberative-process exemption is discretionary rather than mandatory — the agency could have released the material and chose not to — and applying it to all 148 pages without a single line of releasable content drew criticism as excessive. Fact-checkers who asked CDC to explain the redaction reported receiving no answer. But the withheld pages were internal correspondence, not the study itself, and the underlying research was published: Kracalik and colleagues, writing as the Myocarditis Outcomes After mRNA COVID-19 Vaccination Investigators and the CDC COVID-19 Response Team, reported in The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health (2022) that of patients reassessed at least 90 days after onset most were 'considered recovered from myocarditis by their health-care provider, although at the last health-care provider follow-up, 104 (26%) of 393 patients were prescribed daily medication related to myocarditis,' and cautioned that the findings 'might not be generalisable given the small sample size.' One thing the reel gestures at and does not establish, but which does hold up on checking: the MOVING project's published output appears to end there. CDC's project page, last updated September 23, 2022 and now retired to its archive, said the agency 'will contact people with myocarditis reported to VAERS after at least 90 days have passed since myocarditis symptoms began and will publish data as it becomes available,' and describes no follow-up beyond that 90-day window. The reporter who filed the FOIA said at the time that the team planned a further study with updated findings. No such follow-on MOVING paper is indexed in the literature — which is a search result rather than proof that none exists.

notes: Speaker attribution is off the capture's own frames, not inferred: the on-screen nameplate reads Sen. Janae Shamp at the 12:25 PM timestamp (the 'I asked research to print the study for me' passage — she chairs the committee and has Senate research staff) and Dr. Peter McCullough at 12:26 PM (the 'colossal consumer product safety debacle' passage). Both are confirmed committee members in the azleg minutes. The minutes do not itemize the redacted document, which appears to have come up in Shamp's comments or her Attachment C slides; the audio archive is on file with the Secretary of the Senate. Deliberately written to refuse both easy readings. Against the reel: the 148 pages were not 'a study,' the study was published two years earlier, and 'what good does a study do if there's nothing there' has an answer. Against the standard fact-check: (b)(5) is a discretionary exemption, a blanket application across every page of every document is a real and criticised choice, and 'it was properly exempt' is not the same as 'nothing was withheld that could have been released.' The Lancet findings are quoted including the 26%-still-medicated figure and the authors' own generalisability caveat rather than only the recovery headline. PMID confirmed via Europe PMC after an initial wrong-PMID lookup. | 2026-08-02 verification pass. (1) The surfacing clip was checked against the source: the official Arizona Legislature recording was located through the Invintus player API, the audio window around the 12:25 PM on-screen timestamp was pulled and transcribed, and Shamp's and McCullough's words match the reel almost verbatim. The reel is a faithful excerpt, not an edited one — worth stating because a clipped hearing video is exactly the kind of artifact that usually is trimmed. Context the clip cuts: Shamp's remarks run on from a complaint about Pfizer alumni on a federal advisory council, and McCullough continues past the cut into the Pfizer FOIA fight, where he gives the figure as 55 years (our [[2021-pfizer-papers-001]] records the 500-pages-per-month pace that works out to roughly 75 years; both figures circulate and that record is the precise one). (2) The 148-page production itself was NOT obtained. The link circulated in March 2024 was a t.co shortlink that no longer resolves, the Epoch Times copy is paywalled, and no DocumentCloud or Scribd mirror surfaced. Everything here about the document's contents rests on the reporting, not on our own read of the PDF. (3) Searched for a follow-on MOVING publication and found none indexed; stated in the claim as a search result, not as proof of absence.
